canonical_statement: For n > 0 and algebraic real numbers alpha_0,...,alpha_(n-1) such that 1,alpha_0,...,alpha_(n-1) are linearly independent over Q, for every epsilon > 0 only finitely many positive integers q satisfy product_i ||q alpha_i|| < q^(-1-epsilon), where ||x|| is distance to the nearest integer.

canonical_formal_target.status: legacy discovery candidate; exact rev-5.6 elaboration and fingerprint are deferred to S56-M-0401-STATEMENT

domain_and_universes: n : Nat; alpha : Fin n -> Real; q : Nat; epsilon : Real; no polymorphic universes
quantifiers: Q-linear independence of 1 and all alpha i
hypotheses: each alpha_i is algebraic over Q
conclusion: The set of positive natural denominators q satisfying the stated product inequality is finite.
